q-6047.name: Question 1
q-6047.problem: The displacement $s$ of a particle moving in a straight line is given by $s(t)=12{t}^{4}-3{t}^{3}+t.$ Find the particle's acceleration at time $t.$
q-6047.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $v(t)$ by differentiating $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(12{t}^{4}-3{t}^{3}+t) \\  & =48{t}^{3}-9{t}^{2}+1\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we differentiate $v(t)$ to find $a(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(48{t}^{3}-9{t}^{2}+1) \\  & =144{t}^{2}-18t\end{aligned}
$$

q-6047.html:
Question 1
?

The displacement s of a particle moving in a straight line is given by s(t)=12t4−3t3+t. Find the particle's acceleration at time t.

a
a(t)=8t2−t
b
a(t)=48t3−9t2+1
c
a(t)=16t3−3t2+1
d
a(t)=12t55−3t44+t22
e
a(t)=144t2−18t
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we calculate v(t) by differentiating s(t): v(t)=dsdt=ddt(12t4−3t3+t)=48t3−9t2+1

Now, we differentiate v(t) to find a(t): a(t)=dvdt=ddt(48t3−9t2+1)=144t2−18t

q-7180.name: Question 2
q-7180.problem: The displacement $s$ of a particle moving in a straight line is given by $s(t)=\frac{7}{{t}^{3}}+{t}^{2}.$ Find the particle's acceleration at time $t.$
q-7180.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $v(t)$ by differentiating $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{7}{{t}^{3}}+{t}^{2}) \\  & =-\frac{21}{{t}^{4}}+2t\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we differentiate $v(t)$ to find $a(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{21}{{t}^{4}}+2t) \\  & =\frac{84}{{t}^{5}}+2\end{aligned}
$$

q-7180.html:
Question 2
?

The displacement s of a particle moving in a straight line is given by s(t)=7t3+t2. Find the particle's acceleration at time t.

a
a(t)=84t5+2
b
a(t)=7t3+t2
c
a(t)=−21t5+2
d
a(t)=−21t4+2t
e
a(t)=84t5+4t
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we calculate v(t) by differentiating s(t):

v(t)=dsdt=ddt(7t3+t2)=−21t4+2t

Now, we differentiate v(t) to find a(t): a(t)=dvdt=ddt(−21t4+2t)=84t5+2

q-102616.name: Question 4
q-102616.problem: The velocity $v$ (in $\text{m/s}$) of a particle at time $t$ (in seconds) is given by $v(t)=(t\operatorname{ln}⁡t+4t).$ Calculate the velocity of the particle when the acceleration $a$ is equal to $6\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$
q-102616.worked_solution:
We differentiate $v(t)$ to calculate $a(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{ln}⁡t+4t) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡t+1+4 \\  & =5+\operatorname{ln}⁡t\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate the time when the acceleration is $a=6,$ we substitute this into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}6 & =5+\operatorname{ln}⁡t \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡t & =1 \\ {e}^{(\operatorname{ln}⁡t)} & ={e}^{1} \\ t & =e\end{aligned}
$$

Then, to calculate the velocity at time $t=e,$ we substitute this into the equation for the velocity:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(e) & =(e\operatorname{ln}⁡e+4e) \\  & =e(1)+4e \\  & =5e\text{ m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity when $a=6\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}$ is $5e\text{ m/s}.$

Question 4
?

The velocity v (in m/s) of a particle at time t (in seconds) is given by v(t)=(tln⁡t+4t). Calculate the velocity of the particle when the acceleration a is equal to 6m/s2.

a
e m/s
b
5 m/s
c
4 m/s
d
4e m/s
e
5e m/s
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We differentiate v(t) to calculate a(t): a(t)=dvdt=ddt(tln⁡t+4t)=ln⁡t+1+4=5+ln⁡t

To calculate the time when the acceleration is a=6, we substitute this into the above:

6=5+ln⁡tln⁡t=1e(ln⁡t)=e1t=e

Then, to calculate the velocity at time t=e, we substitute this into the equation for the velocity: v(e)=(eln⁡e+4e)=e(1)+4e=5e m/s

Therefore, the velocity when a=6m/s2 is 5e m/s.
